title: Analects — the Chinese text
author: confucius
attributionNote: The recorded sayings of Confucius (Kong Qiu, 551–479 BCE) and his disciples, collected by their followers over the following two centuries. The library follows the received twenty-book arrangement.
description: The Analects is the foundational record of Confucian teaching: brief exchanges in which the Master answers disciples, rulers and critics on learning, ritual, filial piety and government, and in which he appears as often uncertain as authoritative. Its twenty books were assembled by several hands and became one of the Four Books of the later examination canon.
historicalContext: Sayings attributed to Confucius circulated orally and in small collections through the Warring States period; the twenty-book text was established in the Han dynasty and fixed by the commentaries of He Yan and Zhu Xi. This record is the Chinese text alone, as the Chinese Text Project transcribes and punctuates it.
availabilityNote: Complete in the Chinese Text Project's transcription: 20 books, 503 paragraphs, streamed from ctext.org one book at a time. This is the original Chinese, not a translation. When the site cannot be read, the chapter is served from the library's validated import cache.
